html:
The Coahuiltecans were many small bands of hunter-gatherers in the dry brush country of northeast Mexico and south Texas, between the Rio Grande and the Gulf coast. They spoke several languages, perhaps unrelated, which scholars group as Coahuiltecan.

They moved through the seasons gathering prickly pear fruit, mesquite beans, roots and nuts, and hunting deer and rabbits. Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca lived among bands of the region in the 1530s and described them. Spanish missions, above all those at San Antonio from 1718, drew many in, while Apache and later Comanche raids pushed from the north. Disease and these pressures broke them up, and by 1886 only a few speakers of their languages could be found. Their neighbours included the Karankawa on the coast and the Tamaulipecos to the south.
